title: Review last night's aggregations on eight sources before any account is deleted
situation: Halden Example Co (a fictional company) runs SailPoint Identity Security Cloud (ISC). Last night ISC aggregated, that is read the accounts from, eight connected sources: Active Directory, an LDAP (Lightweight Directory Access Protocol) directory and a contractor portal on the head-office virtual appliance (VA) cluster, a finance database through a JDBC (Java Database Connectivity) connector on a branch-office cluster, two SaaS (software as a service) applications, and two sources fed by CSV (comma-separated values) file uploads. Someone uploaded the badge system's CSV this morning, the LDAP export looks short, the video meetings source's API (application programming interface) token expired and the branch-office VA has been offline since a network change. Before anyone trusts the results, the operations manager wants each source checked: what changed, what was correlated to whom, and whether anything would be wrongly deleted.
your_task: Check each source's connector type and connection: a VA-based connector needs a healthy source cluster, a SaaS connector needs valid credentials, and a file source needs a valid file.
For every source that could be read, compare the new accounts with the ones ISC already holds and sort them into new, changed, unchanged and removed.
Apply the account delete threshold: if a run would remove more than the allowed percentage of accounts, or returned no accounts at all, it must be cancelled with nothing deleted.
Correlate the new and changed accounts to identities using each source's attribute pairs in order, keep manual correlations, and flag accounts that match no identity or more than one.

List the entitlements that were newly discovered or are gone from each source, and for every failed source say where to look: the Virtual Appliances page, Test Connection and source health, the source's Import Data history, or Search for the aggregation events.
why_it_matters: Aggregation is how ISC knows who has access. A half-written export or an empty CSV that is trusted as 'everyone left' can delete hundreds of accounts and their access history in one run, and a bad correlation gives one person's access to another. The delete threshold and a careful review are what stop a data problem from becoming an outage or an audit finding.
done_when: Every source has an outcome: COMPLETED, ABORTED_DELETE_THRESHOLD or AGGREGATION_FAILED, with the reason.
No account was deleted by a failed connection, an empty file or a run above its delete threshold.
Every processed account is CORRELATED, UNCORRELATED or AMBIGUOUS, and every uncorrelated or ambiguous account is on the review list for manual correlation.
Every failed source has a named next place to look and an owner to fix it.

glossary.Identity Security Cloud (ISC): SailPoint's cloud identity governance platform, formerly called IdentityNow.
glossary.Source: A connected system, such as Active Directory or a SaaS app, that ISC reads accounts and entitlements from.
glossary.Aggregation: Reading the accounts (or the entitlements) from a source into ISC.
glossary.Correlation: Linking an account to the identity that owns it by matching an account attribute, such as employeeID, with an identity attribute, such as employeeId.
glossary.Optimized aggregation: An aggregation that only processes accounts that changed since the last run; turn optimization off after changing correlation so every account is processed.
glossary.Account delete threshold: The percentage of a source's accounts that one aggregation may remove; above it ISC cancels the aggregation and deletes nothing.
glossary.Virtual appliance (VA): A SailPoint virtual machine inside your own network that runs connectors for systems the cloud cannot reach directly; VAs are grouped into source clusters.
glossary.Entitlement: A permission on a source, such as an Active Directory group or an application role.

talking_point: Reviewed eight overnight ISC aggregations: 3 completed (4 new, 5 changed and 14 unchanged accounts, 4 of them skipped by optimized aggregation, and 1 leaver deleted exactly at Active Directory's 10 % threshold), 2 cancelled by the delete safety rules (an empty badge CSV and an LDAP export missing 37.5 % of accounts against a 20 % threshold), preventing 9 wrong deletions, and 3 failed (a VA cluster offline, an expired API token, a connection timeout) with the place to look for each; correlated 15 accounts, sent 3 uncorrelated and 1 ambiguous rehire match to manual review, and found 2 new entitlements and 1 removed one.
